exports.name: NavigationDirection
exports.description:
PT04 — Navigation direction (contracts/page-transitions.md §4, research R3).

With the Navigation API, every `navigate` event decides the direction from history entry indexes (never
from URLs): push → forward, replace/reload → replace, traverse → back or forward by comparing
`destination.index` with `currentEntry.index`. The tracker writes `data-neshel-pt-direction` on `<html>`
synchronously in the event — before any router updates the DOM — so CSS and React's own view transitions
see it. A `replace` to the current URL is router state bookkeeping and leaves the direction alone. Without the API, routers may call `set()`; otherwise the direction stays `"unknown"` and
direction-aware effects use their neutral variant. One shared listener, reference-counted.

exports.name: usePageTransition
exports.description:
Router-free page transitions: `start(update, options)` runs `update` (a state change) inside a React
Transition with transition types when React manages view transitions, so React captures the real commit;
otherwise inside `startPageTransition`, whose update resolves at the next commit of the component that
called this hook (its layout effect) — or after `maxWait`, when the browser stops holding rendering.
exports.signature: (): { start(update: () => void, options?: StartOptions | undefined): void; }

exports.name: useRouteTransition
exports.description:
Router-independent contract (PT10): coordinates with the COMMITTED location (a layout effect after React
committed the new route, never a click), moves focus only after a push/replace commit to an element the
application marked, and reports the direction. Never intercepts links or history events.
exports.signature: ({ location, type, focus }: RouteTransitionInput): { direction: NavigationDirection; }
